Nucleotide diversity (pi) from iSNV frequencies

Source: R/diversity.R
piISNV.Rd

Estimates nucleotide diversity following Nei & Li (1979), adapted for deep sequencing allele frequencies: $$\pi = \frac{n}{n-1} \cdot \frac{2}{L} \sum_i p_i(1 - p_i)$$ where \(p_i\) is the alternative allele frequency at site \(i\), \(L\) is the genome length, and \(n\) is the number of reads sampled at a site, for which mean read depth stands in. The \(n/(n-1)\) correction removes the finite-sample bias of estimating a frequency from \(n\) draws (Nei 1987, Eq. 10.5). This is a different use of "sample size" from the one in tajimaD, where reads must not stand in for independent lineages. When meanDepth is not provided, the uncorrected estimator is returned (equivalent to infinite sample size).

Usage

piISNV(freq, genomeLength, meanDepth = NULL)

Arguments

freq

Numeric vector. Alternative allele frequencies, between 0 and 1; anything else is an error. NA values are dropped.

genomeLength

Integer scalar. Reference genome length in bp.

meanDepth

Numeric scalar (optional). Mean read depth for finite-sample correction. If NULL, no correction is applied.

Value

Numeric scalar. Nucleotide diversity.

References

Nei M, Li WH (1979). Mathematical model for studying genetic variation in terms of restriction endonucleases. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 76:5269-5273. doi:10.1073/pnas.76.10.5269

Nei M (1987). Molecular Evolutionary Genetics. Columbia University Press, New York. Chapter 10.

Examples

piISNV(c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5), genomeLength = 13588)
#> [1] 8.095378e-05
piISNV(c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5), genomeLength = 13588, meanDepth = 1000)
#> [1] 8.103482e-05
